﻿ the matrix render incorrectly or fail the row-count check; this is mitigated by verifying the table immediately after
 writing. A minor risk is encoding artifacts, since the Write tool's output on Windows could theoretically introduce a
 byte-order mark or line-ending surprises; the V07 check exists specifically to catch this. Overall none of these risks
 affect anything beyond the single new file.

 Rollback

 Rollback is trivial because the change consists solely of one newly created file. If the file is judged unnecessary or
 incorrect, delete verification-matrix.md from the project root, which restores the directory exactly to its prior
 empty state. No configuration, registry, environment, or other-file changes need to be reverted, and no process
 restarts or cache clears are required. Since the directory is not a git repository, deletion is the complete and
 sufficient rollback mechanism, and it can be performed at any time with a single Remove-Item command.

 Verification of this plan's implementation

 After writing the file, run checks V01–V08exactly as specified in the matrix (Glob/Read for structure, Grep for
 heading and placeholder absence, Read-based row/cell counts, and a PowerShell hex dump for encoding). All eight rows
 must read pass in the Status column before reporting success; any fail is corrected and re-verified per step 7 above.
